speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by clarifying the timeline: exactly how many months or years have passed since your tympanoplasty surgery? Additionally, does this shooting pain occur when you touch the outer ear or only when pressure is applied to the eardrum area?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since the pain occurs specifically when eating and you have a history of ear infections, could you describe exactly where you feel this "shooting" sensation—is it deep inside the ear canal, behind your ear, or radiating to your jaw or teeth? Also, do you notice any changes in your jaw movement or any clicking sounds when you chew?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-tympanoplasty Glomus Tympanicum Tumor. 

Given the combination of shooting ear pain triggered by eating, the history of recurrent ear infections, and the specific discomfort with earrings suggesting a mass effect on the tympanic membrane, this clinical picture is highly suspicious for a Glomus Tympanicum tumor rather than simple granulation tissue or nerve entrapment.
